I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea.

Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: The user wants to log food items. They mention 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier they had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We need to log each item. The function log_food expects food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We need to decide portion_unit for each. For mango pieces: unit "piece". Portion_amount 8. For chai tea: maybe "cup" or "tablespoon"? Usually tea is a cup. So portion_unit "cup" and portion_amount 1? But they didn't specify amount. We can assume 1 cup. For pepperoni pizza slices: unit "slice", portion_amount 2. For coffee: maybe "cup" or "tablespoon"? Usually coffee is a cup. So portion_amount 1 cup. We need to log each separately. We can call function multiple times. The user didn't specify meal_type. We can default to snack. But we can also guess: mango and chai tea could be breakfast? But not sure. We'll just use default snack. Also log_date: we can use current date/time. But we don't have that. We can leave null. We'll just call function with default. We'll produce separate calls.
